result:
I fixed the "Load more" bug in `src/server/repositories/_paging.ts`. All 617 tests pass, but I didn't add a test that pages through entries sharing a timestamp. So the specific case the customer hit is fixed in the code but not covered by any test.

**Cause:** each list is sorted newest first, with the entry's ID used to order entries that share a timestamp. But the query that fetches the next page only asked for entries "older than" the last timestamp shown. When several entries were recorded at the same moment and a page ended in the middle of that group, the rest of the group was never fetched. That's why the header count was right but the pages came up short. Entries created one at a time have different timestamps, so those lists paged correctly.

**Fix:** the next-page query now also includes entries with the *same* timestamp and a lower ID. That matches the sort order exactly, so paging with any page size returns every entry once, in the same order as one large page. Every list that uses this shared helper is fixed, including the project issue list, notification inbox and audit log. The workspace filter is applied separately and is unchanged, so pages still only include the current workspace's entries.
